title: The Cyclone, part 2
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: Uncle Henry never laughed. He worked hard from morning till night and did not know what joy was. He was gray also, from his long beard to his rough boots, and he looked stern and solemn, and rarely spoke.

It was Toto that made Dorothy laugh, and saved her from growing as gray as her other surroundings. Toto was not gray; he was a little black dog, with long silky hair and small black eyes that twinkled merrily on either side of his funny, wee nose. Toto played all day long, and Dorothy played with him, and loved him dearly.

Today, however, they were not playing. Uncle Henry sat upon the doorstep and looked anxiously at the sky, which was even grayer than usual. Dorothy stood in the door with Toto in her arms, and looked at the sky too. Aunt Em was washing the dishes.

From the far north they heard a low wail of the wind, and Uncle Henry and Dorothy could see where the long grass bowed in waves before the coming storm. There now came a sharp whistling in the air from the south, and as they turned their eyes that way they saw ripples in the grass coming from that direction also.
“There’s a cyclone coming, Em,” he called to his wife. “I’ll go look after the stock.” Then he ran toward the sheds where the cows and horses were kept.
Aunt Em dropped her work and came to the door. One glance told her of the danger close at hand.
“Quick, Dorothy!” she screamed. “Run for the cellar!”

Toto jumped out of Dorothy’s arms and hid under the bed, and the girl started to get him. Aunt Em, badly frightened, threw open the trap door in the floor and climbed down the ladder into the small, dark hole. Dorothy caught Toto at last and started to follow her aunt. When she was halfway across the room there came a great shriek from the wind, and the house shook so hard that she lost her footing and sat down suddenly upon the floor.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what kind of dog is Toto?
options: A little black dog with long silky hair
A large gray dog with short rough hair
A little brown dog with a curled tail
A small white dog with black markings

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what was Aunt Em doing as the sky grew grayer?
options: Washing the dishes
Feeding the horses
Mending the roof
Sweeping the floor

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did Uncle Henry go once he saw the storm coming?
options: To the sheds where the cows and horses were kept
Down the ladder into the small dark cyclone cellar
Out to the long grass to watch the wind arrive
Into the house to fetch Dorothy and the dog

questions.prompt: Per the passage, where did Toto hide when Dorothy was told to run?
options: Under the bed
In the cupboard
Behind the stove
Down the trap door

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the narrator say Toto saved Dorothy from growing gray?
options: He gave her something to laugh at in a joyless place
He was the only animal that the farm had left to keep
He kept watch on the sky so that she did not have to
He was the one creature there that had not been sunburned

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did Dorothy not reach the cellar with her aunt?
options: She turned back to catch Toto first
She could not lift the heavy trap door
She was watching the grass from the door
She had been sent out to help her uncle

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does it suggest that one glance told Aunt Em of the danger?
options: She knew the signs of a cyclone at once
She had been warned by a neighbour already
She could see the sheds had been blown down
She had never seen such a sky in her life

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does calling Uncle Henry gray convey?
options: The colour had gone out of the whole man, not just his beard
His clothes had faded from being washed too many times
He had turned pale from the fright the storm gave him
He wore gray because it was the only cloth they had

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures what the passage shows about the household?
options: Hard joyless work, with a small dog the only source of laughter
A cheerful family whose work on the prairie had made them rich
A household so frightened of storms that nobody dared go out
Three people who had run out of things to say to each other

questions.prompt: Which of these best describes the turn the passage takes?
options: An anxious ordinary day breaks into sudden emergency
A long-expected storm arrives exactly as predicted
A quarrel between the family ends in the cellar
A day of play is interrupted by work on the farm

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Uncle Henry call out to his wife?
options: That a cyclone was coming
That the sheds had blown over
That the cellar door was stuck
That the horses had bolted

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did Aunt Em scream to Dorothy?
options: To run for the cellar
To catch hold of Toto
To shut the trap door
To fetch her uncle back

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how are Toto's eyes described?
options: Small and black, twinkling merrily
Large and brown, watching anxiously
Small and gray, like everything else
Bright and blue, set wide apart

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what first warned the family that the wind was rising?
options: A low wail from the north and grass bowing in waves
A sudden darkness that fell across the whole prairie
The cows and horses growing restless in their sheds
A neighbour riding over to tell them what was coming

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what do Uncle Henry's silence and solemn look suggest about his life?
options: Years of hard labour had worn the pleasure out of it
He had quarrelled with his wife and would not speak
He was troubled by something he refused to explain
He had never learned to talk easily with children

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does Uncle Henry mean by the stock?
options: The farm animals in his care
The stores of food for the winter
The wooden posts of the fences
The goods he keeps to sell

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A gray household is overtaken by a storm before it can shelter
A family argues about whether the coming storm is dangerous
A girl and her dog are left alone on the farm for the day
A farmer works through a storm to save his cows and horses
